questions.passage: In what is now Washington state, the Tulalip Tribes operate the Hibulb Cultural Center. The Citizen Potawatomi Nation, a tribe in Oklahoma, employs a similar strategy in its own cultural center. questions.prompt: Which best describes the overall structure of the text?

questions.passage: Luang Prabang has high pedestrian traffic, but simply replicating a feature of Luang Prabang associated with walkability—e.g., its human-scaled architecture—may be insufficient to induce increased walking in other cities. As urbanist Mariela Alfonzo argues, our understanding of individuals’ decision-making about whether to walk is insufficiently robust: some studies emphasize the role of local norms, others the role of demographic characteristics, and so on, but walking decisions are made in complex context in which multiple conditions and needs inform individuals’ choices.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe the effect of human-scaled architecture on any given city’s walkability.
choices.B: To explain why it is challenging to compare the amount of pedestrian traffic in different cities.
choices.C: To present a claim about how individuals’ decision-making about walking can be improved.
choices.D: To discuss the difficulty of identifying a reliable way to increase walking in any given city.

questions.passage: In Hoocak, an Indigenous language from the Mid-Atlantic region of what is now the United States, okayeke means “bad,” whereas ati okayeye’tesel means “bad houses.” This phenomenon, in which an element of a root word is repeated, sometimes with modification, within another word that is related to the root word, is called reduplication. In this case, the element “ye” in okayeke gets repeated in ati okayeye’tesel. There are many examples of this type of reduplication in Hoocak.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined part?

choices.C: It acknowledges that Hoocak has some important exceptions to the general pattern described earlier.
choices.D: It emphasizes how frequently reduplication occurs in Hoocak.

questions.passage: Veronica L. Bura, Akito Y. Kawahara, and Jayne E. Yack investigated the evolution and function of sound production in silk moth and hawk moth caterpillars. They found that during harmless simulated attacks on isolated caterpillars, 33% of the tested species produced sound, which ranged from clicks in Manduca pellenia to whistles in Rhodinia fugax. choices.D: some hoards were found as a result of artifacts being dug up by accident.

questions.passage:
Text 1
For decades ornithologists assumed that if they saw a singing Bell’s vireo—a bird species found in temperate North America—they must be observing a male. That’s because birdsong has long been considered a male trait; researchers have argued that singing enables males to attract mates and claim territory.
Text 2
Recent evidence shows that a female Bell’s vireo is as capable of song as a male is. In fact, Kara J. Odom and colleagues found evidence of female song in 71% of the 323 species they examined. They claim that the historical mischaracterization of birdsong as a male trait is largely the result of bias: much of the research ornithologists have carried out has been near universities in the temperate northern hemisphere, where female birdsong is less common than it is in the tropics.
questions.prompt: Based on the texts, how would Odom and colleagues (Text 2) most likely respond to the view of birdsong presented in Text 1?

choices.B: They would claim that other factors than mate attraction and territorial defense have driven the evolution of singing in male birds.
choices.C: They would underscore that male songbirds in temperate zones are likely using their songs for different purposes than are male songbirds in the tropics.
choices.D: They would argue that it was influenced by the kinds of study sites researchers tended to select.

A run-of-river hydroelectric power plant, as the name suggests, uses the natural flow of a water source to generate electricity but is unable to start or stop that flow through its generators.
